chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman performing Tamattu' Hajj whose husband consummated the marriage with her before she shortened her hair (the ritual act of exiting Ihram). When she feared that he would overpower her, she bent down to her hair and bit off pieces of it with her teeth and cut it with her fingernails. Is there any blame upon her? He said, 'No, not everyone has access to scissors.'

key_terms.تُقَصِّرَ: She shortens (her hair, the ritual act of exiting Ihram)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعَةٍ: A woman performing Tamattu' Hajj (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.هَلْ عَلَيْهَا شَيْءٌ: Is there any blame/penalty upon her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman in Ihram cuts her hair with her teeth or nails because she has no scissors?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the obligation to cut hair for exiting Ihram is flexible regarding the method, emphasizing that the lack of conventional tools like scissors does not invalidate the act or incur penalty. This ruling underscores the principle of ease (yusr) in Shia jurisprudence, where natural alternatives are deemed sufficient when standard instruments are unavailable, reflecting the practical adaptability of ritual law.
